name: Jeroboam
overview: Jeroboam was a male from the tribe of Ephraim, known as Solomon's servant and the son of Nebat. He rebelled against King Solomon as recorded in 1 Kings 11:26 and was later established as king over Israel (1 Kings 12:20). This significant transition marks him as a pivotal figure in the division of the united monarchy.
namesAndTitles: The name Jeroboam means 'the people increase,' reflecting perhaps a hope for growth or strength among the people. He is also referred to by the titles 'King Jeroboam' and 'King of Israel,' which emphasize his royal status and authority over the northern kingdom, as noted in 1 Kings 15:1 and 1 Kings 15:9 respectively.
familyAndRelationships: Jeroboam was the son of Nebat and Zeruah as explicitly stated in 1 Kings 11:26. Additionally, he is inferred to be the father of Abijah and Nadab, based on references in 1 Kings 14:1 and 1 Kings 14:20. These relationships place him within a familial line that continued his royal legacy in Israel.
scriptureSignificance: Jeroboam's significance in Scripture lies in his role as the leader who rebelled against Solomon and became the first king of the northern kingdom of Israel after the kingdom's division. His rise marks a critical moment in Israel's history, demonstrating the fulfillment of God's judgment on Solomon's house and the political and spiritual realignment of the nation. His reign set the stage for subsequent developments in Israel's monarchy and covenantal narrative.
